title: RFI’s AlpEW seismic-warning system reportedly stops Rome–Naples trains during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake
summary: RFI’s AlpEW imposes train restrictions from seismic signals. News reports a stop during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake; the technical paper verifies neither that episode nor a learned AI model.
account: ANSA reported on 14 Jul 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system. It is on the Rome-Naples high-speed line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. euronews (15 Jul 2025) added that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by an SDH fiber network. An advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the quake's danger, per euronews. The system had been operational since 3 May 2025. In the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. During it, trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. Neither article gives the date of that earthquake. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the system as AI-powered and a protective response.
purpose: The system is built to detect the first seismic waves and automatically slow or stop high-speed trains before stronger shaking arrives.
system: AlpEW (Array lineare per Early Warning), RFI’s seismic early-warning platform for the Rome–Naples high-speed railway.
developer: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II and JR RTRI
taxonomy_note: An automatic train stop on P-wave detection is a failsafe; no harm averted is documented.

ratings.reason: Precautionary stops were executed automatically during a magnitude 4.4 quake. No damage, derailment or delay figures are reported.
No passenger outcome is documented beyond the stops.

ai_role.statement: The original developer study describes AlpEW as signal processing with empirical ground-motion prediction and probabilistic alert thresholds. Filter Picker detects transients, Train Marker distinguishes train vibration from seismic signals, and railway controls impose restrictions automatically. The authors discuss machine learning as a possible alternative, but do not establish a learned AI model in the deployed system. The study’s operational observations cover March 2020–January 2022 and do not verify the M 4.4 stop reported in 2025 news coverage.

fields.account: ANSA reported on 14 Jul 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system. It is on the Rome-Naples high-speed line. It was developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II. Technical support came from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways. A network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves. Within seconds it automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. euronews (15 Jul 2025) added that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes. They are linked by an SDH fiber network. An advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the quake's danger, per euronews. The system had been operational since 3 May 2025. In the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. During it, trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. Neither article gives the date of that earthquake. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the system as AI-powered and a protective response.

They are linked by an SDH fiber network. An advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the quake's danger, per euronews. The system had been operational since 3 May 2025. In the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. During it, trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. Neither article gives the date of that earthquake. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the system as AI-powered and a protective response.
